title: Production and characterization of cell-penetrating recombinant botulinum neurotoxin type A
protocol: Set up the PCR reaction using an insect cell codon-optimized synthesized BoNTA gene.
Perform restriction digestion on the PCR product.
Extract gel fragments of the digested products.
Ligate the purified DNA fragments into pFastBac1 vector.
Transform competent E. coli cells with the ligation mixture.
Culture transformed bacteria and purify plasmid DNA.
Set up PCR reactions in 8-tube strips.
Collect the PCR product using MinElute PCR Purification Kit (Qiagen).
Elute the DNA using 10 μL of water.
Store eluted DNA at −20°C for one week.
Digest pFastBac1 vector and PCR products with XbaI and HindIII.
Incubate the reaction at 37°C for 3 h, and then add calf intestinal alkaline phosphatase (CIP) of 0.5 μL for further incubation for 30 min.
Mix digestion products with 10 μL of 6× DNA loading dye.
Prepare a 1% (wt/vol) agarose gel with Tris acetate-EDTA (TAE) buffer.
Run the gel at 100 volts for 45 minutes.
Cut the desired band from the agarose gel.
Dissolve the cut gel in one volume binding buffer (XP2) for 7 minutes at 60°C.
Run the solubilized gel through a HiBind DNA Mini Column according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Elute DNA using 20 μL of water.
Store purified digestion products at −20°C for one week.
Ligate enzyme-treated PCR product and pFastBac1 vector with an insert-to-vector molar ratio of 3:1.
Incubate the reaction at 16°C for 12–16 hours.
Thaw Trelief 5α Chemically Competent Cells on ice.
Gently mix cells with 10 μL of ligation reaction product from step 4.
Keep the mixture on ice for 15 minutes.
Heat-shock the mixture at 42°C for 90 seconds using a water bath.
Incubate the heat-shocked mixture on ice for 3 minutes.
Transfer cell suspension to a culture tube containing 0.5 mL of LB medium.
Incubate the cells with shaking at 200 g for 1 hour at 37°C.
Spread 200 μL of bacterial cell culture on LB agar plates with 50 μg/mL kanamycin.
Incubate the plates at 37°C for 12–16 hours.
Prepare growth medium (LB medium containing 50 μg/mL kanamycin).
Add 5 mL of growth medium in 14 mL round bottom test tubes.
Inoculate each tube with a single colony from a successful transformation.
Grow bacterial culture for 12–16 hours in a 37°C incubator at 225 rpm.
Collect bacteria by centrifugation at 5000 g for 10 minutes.
Extract plasmid harboring the gene of interest using Qiagen plasmid miniprep kit according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Confirm plasmid identity by DNA sequencing.
Store purified plasmids at -20°C for long-term use.
Dispense 100 μL of cells into 1.5 mL tubes.
Add approximately 1 μg recombinant donor plasmid in 5 μL ddH2O and gently mix by tapping the tube.
Incubate the mixture on ice for 30 min.
Heat shock the mixture at 42°C water bath for 45 s.
Chill the mixture on ice for 2 min.
Add 500 μL LB to the mixture.
Place the mixture in a shaking incubator at 37°C with a shaking speed of 225 rpm for 4 h.
Dilute 20 μL transposition mixture with 100 μL LB.
Place 120 μL of each dilution on plates and spread evenly over the surface.
Incubate for 24–48 h at 37°C.
Pick white single colony and inoculate into 5 mL LB medium supplemented with 50 μg/mL kanamycin, 7 μg/mL gentamicin, and 10 μg/mL tetracycline in 14 mL round bottom test tubes.
Grow at 37°C to stationary phase (16–24 h) with shaking at 250–300 rpm.
Pick up two white colonies for bacmid isolation.
Harvest cells and resuspend cell pellet with 250 μL Buffer P1 from the Qiagen Plasmid Mini Kit, then transfer the resuspension into a transparent 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Lyse the cells with 250 μL Buffer P2 followed by neutralization using 350 μL of Buffer N3.
After neutralization, spin at around 16,000 g for 10 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant (∼800 μL) to a transparent 1.5 mL tube by careful pipetting.
Spin the supernatant at 16,000 g for 3 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant (∼720 μL) to a transparent 1.5 mL tube by careful pipetting.
Add 500 μL isopropanol and thoroughly mix the solution.
Spin the mixture for 10 min at 16,000 g at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant by pipetting carefully.
Add 200 μL cold 70% ethanol to wash the pellet.
Spin for 5 min at 16,000 g at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant by pipetting carefully with a 200 μL tip.
Gently add 50 μL cold 70% ethanol.
Bring the closed tubes containing the bacmids in 70% ethanol into a sterile laminar flow cabinet.
Remove the 50 μL 70% ethanol by pipetting carefully.
Air-dry the pellets for 10 min.
Maintain a sterile environment during the transfection process.
Ensure ethanol is completely removed from bacmid samples.
Add 30 μL of sterile water to each tube containing DNA pellets.
Resuspend DNA pellets by gently tapping the tubes.
Seed 0.5–1.0 × 10^6 insect cells into a 6-well plate and incubate at 27°C for 15 min before transfection.
Prepare solution A: add 10 μL FuGENE transfection agent to 100 μL Sf-900 II serum-free medium.
Prepare solution B: add 25 μL bacmid into 200 μL Sf-900 II serum-free medium.
Mix solutions A and B and incubate at 25°C for 15–30 min.
Add the mixed solution A-B to the seeded Sf9 culture drop by drop.
Maintain a final medium volume of 2.5–3.0 mL after transfection.
Swirl the 6-well plate gently after transfection to ensure even distribution of the cells.
Incubate the transfected 6-well plates at 27°C in the dark.
Check the cells every day for contamination and viability.
Centrifuge the medium supernatant at 1,000 g for 10 min at 4°C after 72 hours to remove cell debris.
Harvest the supernatant as initial virus (P1) and store at 4°C in dark for immediate use or at −20°C in dark for long-term use.
Seed insect cells with viability of more than 95% into 125 mL shake flasks containing Sf-900 II serum-free medium at a density of 1–1.5 × 10^6/mL.
Add 2 mL P1 viral stock to suspension Sf9 cells in the shake flasks.
Incubate the cells in a 27°C incubator with a stirring rate of 120 rpm.
Count and record cell density and viability at 72 hours post-infection.
Collect the medium containing virus (P2) from shaker flasks after 72 hours.
Centrifuge the virus-containing medium at 500 g for 5 min at 4°C to remove cells and large debris.
Store the P2 at 4°C in dark for immediate use or at −20°C in dark for long-term use.
Seed insect cells with viability of more than 95% into 250 mL shake flasks containing Sf-900 II serum-free medium at a density of 1–1.5 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Add P2 viral stock (1% v/v) to suspension Sf9 cells.
Incubate the cells in a 27°C incubator with a stirring rate of 120 rpm.
Count and record cell density and viability at 72 h post-infection.
Collect the medium containing virus from shaker flasks.
Centrifuge the virus-containing medium at 500 g for 5 min at 4°C to remove cells and large debris.
Store the supernatant at 4°C in dark for immediate use or at −20°C in dark for long-term use.
Seed Hi-5 insect cells with viability of more than 95% into 1 L shake flask containing 300 mL ESf 921 Insect Cell Culture Medium at a density of 2 × 10^6 cells/mL.
Add P3 viral stock (1% v/v) to suspension Hi-5 cells.
Incubate the cells in a 27°C incubator with a stirring rate of 120 rpm.
Count and record cell density and viability at 48 h post infection.
Collect the cells by centrifuging the culture at 500 g for 10 min at 4°C to remove supernatant.
Store the cell pellet at −80°C for one year.
Resuspend cell pellet in 50–100 mL Ni-Lysis buffer.
Homogenize the resuspended cells by sonication at 70% power for two cycles of 5 min with 5 s on/5 s off intervals.
Centrifuge the sonicated cells at 16,000 g for 30 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a new tube if necessary and repeat centrifugation.
Add 2 mL Ni-NTA agarose beads (50% slurry) to the supernatant and rotate at 4°C for 1–3 hours.
Wash the beads with 50 mL of Ni-Wash buffer I.
Wash the beads with 50 mL of Ni-Wash buffer II.
Concentrate the flow through to about 3 mL using a 50 MWCO spin concentrator at 4°C.
Wash the beads with 50 mL of Ni-Wash buffer III.
Concentrate the flow through to about 3 mL using a 50 MWCO spin concentrator at 4°C.
Elute the protein with 50 mL of Ni-elution buffer.
Concentrate the eluate to about 3 mL using a 50 MWCO spin concentrator at 4°C.
Equilibrate Superdex 200 resins in a 10/300 GL column with 1.5 CV SEC buffer.
Load 500 μL eluted sample onto Superdex 200 in a 10/300 GL column.
Harvest the target proteins according to UV reads.
Store purified proteins at −80°C for one year.
Evaluate the integrity and purity of CPP-BoNTA proteins before analysis.
Conduct SDS-PAGE analysis of purified CPP-BoNTA proteins.
Transfer the sticker from the GenScript pre-made gel and place it in the gel tank.
Fill the gel tank with 1× MOPS SDS running buffer.
Remove the comb and load 10 μL of protein sample into each well.
Run the gel at 200 V for approximately 30 minutes.
Stain the gel with Coomassie blue staining buffer for 20 minutes.
Destain the gel with destaining buffer for approximately 40 minutes.
Prepare protein samples between 10–50 μg with a purity of more than 90%.
Set up AB SCIEX TripleTOF™ 4600 coupled directly to a Nexera UHPLC LC-30A with an ACE C4 column for all LC-MS/MS analyses.
Configure mobile phase A as H2O with 0.1 FA, and mobile phase B as CH3CN with 0.1 FA.
Set the flow rate to be 0.4 mL/min.
Use Peakviewer software for database searching and spectral interpretation.
Prepare 96-well black microplate.
Add reaction solution containing 1× SNAPtide assay buffer and 10 μM SNAPtide to the plate.
Add CPP-BoNTA proteins to the reaction to achieve a final concentration of 100 nM in a 100 μL reaction solution.
Incubate the reaction at 37°C for 40 min.
Measure the fluorescence using a plate reader with an excitation wavelength of 490 nm and an emission wavelength of 523 nm.
Maintain N2a cells in MEM EARLES supplemented with 10% FBS, 1% MEM NEAA and 100 U/mL penicillin/streptomycin at 37°C in fully humidified atmosphere with 5% CO2.
Coat 12 mm coverslips with 500 μL poly-L-lysine solution (1:10 dilution in water) by incubating at 25°C for 1 h in a 24-well plate.
Wash coverslips three times with sterile PBS and air dry at 4°C for 12–16 h.
Seed N2a cells onto poly-L-lysine-coated coverslips and culture in a 37°C/5% CO2 incubator for additional 2 days until a confluency of 70%-80% is reached.
After 4 h incubation with 100 nM CPP-BoNTA, fix N2a cells with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) at 25°C for 15 min.
Treat cells with PBS containing 0.1% Triton X-100 for 10 min.
Wash cells three times with PBS containing 0.2% BSA.
Block non-specific binding sites with PBS containing 0.2% BSA at 25°C for 30 minutes.
Stain cells with goat anti-FLAG antibody and rabbit anti-SV2A antibodies at a 1 to 200 dilution in PBS supplemented with 0.2% BSA.
Cover the plate at 25°C for 1–2 hours during primary antibody incubation.
Wash coverslips 5 times with PBS supplemented with 0.2% BSA.
Wash coverslips 5 times with PBS.
Wash coverslips 5 times with PBS supplemented with 0.2% BSA.
Stain cells with Alexa568-conjugated donkey anti-rabbit IgG and Alexa488-conjugated donkey anti-goat IgG secondary antibodies in PBS supplemented with 0.2% BSA.
Cover the plate at 25°C for 45 minutes during secondary antibody incubation.
Wash coverslips 5 times with PBS supplemented with 0.2% BSA.
Wash coverslips 5 times with PBS.
Wash coverslips 5 times with PBS supplemented with 0.2% BSA.
Stain antibody-labeled cell sections with Hoechst 33342 for nucleus visualization in PBS at 25°C for 5–10 minutes.
Wash coverslips 3 times with PBS.
Mount the samples.
Prepare microscope slides.
Add coverslips on microscope slides with Prolong gold antifade reagent.
Leave the microscope slides at 25°C to dry in the dark for 12–16 hours.
Store dried microscope slides at 4°C for long-term use.
Visualize samples on a LSM710 laser scanning confocal microscopy system using excitation/emission filters for red and green channels as 493 nm/598 nm and 410 nm/507 nm respectively.
Measure the fluorescence intensity in each cell using ZEN 2011 imaging software (Zeiss).
Subtract background signal from images using the Math function on the FIJI software.
Visualize prepared samples on TissueFAXS fluorescence imaging system.
Scan whole section slices.
Calculate the fluorescence intensity using TissueQuest software.
Prepare 8 to 12-week-old male or female C57BL/6 mice for intramuscular injection.
Attach a 30-gauge needle to a sterile 250 μL Hamilton syringe.
Dispense different doses of CPP-BoNTA according to the body weight of the mice, so that each mouse receives a fixed volume of 5 μL.
Inject CPP-BoNTA or vehicle (0.9% saline) into the head of the right gastrocnemius muscle of mice.
Avoid the needle passing through the gastrocnemius muscle during injection in mice.
Prevent bleeding during the injection; if bleeding occurs, stop it by pushing the wound with an alcohol cotton ball and then wipe off the blood.
Suspend mice briefly by their tails two days after injection to elicit a characteristic startle response for DAS measurement.
Observe and record the shape of the foot and digits of the suspended mouse.

Assign DAS values based on the degree of digit abduction: zero-point for flat foot with no difference in digit spread compared to untreated leg, one-point for slight differences or partial contact between two digits, two-point for slight space open at tips of all digits or three digits touching, three-point for five digits touching if foot is flat or four digits if curved, and four-point for a curved foot with all five digits touching.
Determine the half intramuscular lethal dose (IMLD50) for BoNTA, T-BoNTA and Z-BoNTA proteins.
Set the endpoint of monitoring at day 5 after treatment.
Determine the half intramuscular effective dose (IMED50).
Calculate the intramuscular therapeutic index by dividing IMLD50 by IMED50.
Section fresh gastrocnemius muscles into small pieces.
Fix immediately with 4% paraformaldehyde at 25°C for 10 min.
Dehydrate tissue in 30% sucrose for 12–16 h.
Dry tissue blocks with paper towels.
Place tissue blocks on tissue molds.
Incubate tissue blocks with 100% OCT over a total period of 4 h at -80°C.
Frozen-section OCT-embedded gastrocnemius muscles serially at 10 μm interval along the transverse and longitudinal direction.
Block non-specific binding sites with PBS supplemented with 5% BSA at 25°C for 1 h.
Wash sections 5 times with PBS for 5 min each time.
Incubate slices with goat anti-FLAG antibody and anti-SV2A antibodies diluted 200-fold in PBS supplemented with 0.2% BSA at 4°C for 12–16 h.
Wash the slices 3 times with PBS supplemented with 0.2% BSA.
Wash the slices 3 times with PBS.
Incubate with fluorochrome-conjugated secondary antibody diluted 1000-fold in PBS supplemented with 0.2% BSA for 1 h at 25°C in dark.
Wash the slices 3 times with PBS supplemented with 0.2% BSA.
Wash the slices 3 times with PBS.
Wash the slices 3 times with PBS supplemented with 0.2% BSA.
Incubate with Hoechst 33342 diluted 5,000-fold in PBS for 10 min at 25°C in the dark.
Wash the slices 3 times with PBS.
Prepare microscope slides and add coverslips on microscope slides with Prolong gold antifade reagent.
Coat the edges of the coverslip with a thin layer of clear nail polish.
Leave the coated coverslips to dry in the dark for 12–16 h.
Store the prepared slides at 4°C for long-term use.
Visualize the samples on a LSM710 laser scanning confocal microscopy.
Measure the fluorescence intensity in each cell by ZEN 2011 imaging software.
